::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Find the equation of the tangent line to the curve $3x^3 + 3y^2-11=4xy-x$ at the point $(1,-1)$.](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/1126896/find-the-equation-of-the-tangent-line-to-the-curve-3x3-3y2-11-4xy-x-at-the), asked by [Jeffrey](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/211827/jeffrey) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2015-01-30; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> The answer choices are given below:
>
>  - a) $5x + 7y = -2$
>  - b) $-7x+5y = -12$
>  - c) $-5x + 7y = -12$
>  - d) $7x+5y = - 12$
>  - e) $-7x + 5y = 2$
:::

You want to 

 * implicitly differentiate both sides of the equation 

 * solve the resulting equation for $\frac{dy}{dx}$ as a function of $x$ and $y$

 * evaluate that expression at $(x,y) = (1,-1)$ to find the slope of the line tangent to the curve at $(1,-1)$.

 * Use that slope and the point $(1,-1)$ to find the equation of the line.
